newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian ex-police jailed over West Java riot.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian ex-police jailed over West Java riot.

text.p: Four Indonesian policemen were sentenced to between 10 months and a little over two years for the beating of an Islamic religious teacher which sparked a riot in West Java, the official Antara news agency reported.

The agency said main defendant Corporal Nursamsi Hendri was sentenced to two years and four months, Sergeant Agus Martadinata two years and three months, Sergeant Agus Yulianto one year and 11 months and Sergeant Dedi Haerudin 10 months in jail.

Presiding judge of the military tribunal in the West Java city of Bandung, Colonel Hotma Pakpahan, said in the verdict the defendants were guilty of beating the religious teacher, Mahmud Farid, and two students during interrogation in Tasikmalaya in late December.
The four accused have already been discharged from the police for their actions.
Military prosecutors said the defendants beat the three victims after Hendri's son had been punished for stealing money from other students in a Moslem boarding school where Farid taught.
Reports of the beating spread in Tasikmalaya and a mob of mainly Moslem youths later burned shops, police stations and churches. Four people died in the disturbance.
Authorities have said 22 civilians will soon be tried for taking part in the riot. One of the accused has been charged with subversion, which carries a possible death penalty.
